title: A value the new release takes where an object is made moves there from the setter old code called later
text: GameDiff learns, from how the game's own code builds the same object, that a changed call X (a factory) followed through calls that give the object back by a changed setter Y became X with Y's value (1.21.11: CycleButton.builder(f) ... withInitialValue(v) is builder(f, v); booleanBuilder(a, b) ... withInitialValue(Boolean.valueOf(x)) is booleanBuilder(a, b, x)). JarPort finds the pair by data flow in each method (PortChains, late): Y's receiver is X's value through calls that give it back, each used only by the next, in one straight run of code; Y's value is written again where X is when it can be read there (constants, fields, parameters never stored to, locals stored once before X, getters over those), and Y only drops its value. Y alone is no longer learned as dropped.
finish: port.jar-links.newest up from 16, every update and big updates no lower, load on 26.3 server and client for newly linked standalone mods
wrongIf: a mod whose setter value moved behaves differently in game from its old version
result: 2026-11-21 (on #150): newest 16 -> 17 (NeoForge jump 11 -> 12); every update 6,051 -> 6,056, big updates 1,931 -> 1,936 (1.21.10 -> 1.21.11 Fabric 37 -> 40, NeoForge 48 -> 50), none lower. Mods with these calls unlinked: NeoForge 1.21.10 -> 1.21.11 8 -> 3, the NeoForge jump 13 -> 6. Real games: NeoForge 1.21.11 server 26 of 29 linked mods load, both newly linked (Mouse Tweaks, ShulkerBoxTooltip) among them; pack-check's client does not run 1.21.11 yet. On 26.3 the newly linked Mouse Tweaks loads on the server and fails in the client before its builder code runs: it reads Minecraft.getInstance() while being constructed, and 26.3 makes the Minecraft instance later. call, game: template does not fall to this (one call into a chain is the other direction).
